mainTopic: Why the פסוק of the betrothed נערה uses the words חטא, מות, נער and נערה: which forbidden relations allow saving the victim at the cost of the attacker's life (רודף), and which sins are excluded.
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a צריכותא on the פסוק 'אין לנערה חטא מות'. The word 'חטא' is needed to include all עריות, 'מות' keeps out plain לאוין, and 'חטא' again brings in כריתות. If 'חטא מות' covers everything, the words 'נער' and 'נערה' come to exclude cases: עבודה זרה, בהמה and שבת, where we do not kill a person to stop the sin. The גמרא then shows how רבי שמעון בן יוחי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who do not exclude עבודה זרה or שבת, use these two words. Next it returns to the ברייתא: רבי יהודה says that when the girl tells rescuers 'leave him alone' out of fear, the attacker is not killed. רבא explains that the רבנן base the law on her degradation, while רבי יהודה bases it on her readiness to die. אביי adds that only a big degradation counts, not a widow with a כהן גדול. Finally, the גמרא asks why a brother who rapes his sister pays a קנס if he could be killed. רב חסדא answers with two separate acts, and רבא answers that she gave in, following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Why the word 'sin' is needed to include other forbidden relations
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had taught only about a male victim and a betrothed young woman, we would think only they can be saved at the attacker's life. These two cases are special. So the Torah wrote 'חטא' to include all other עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We might have thought only these two are saved, because for the male it is not his natural way, and the betrothed girl is degraded. But other forbidden women, for whom it is the natural way and who are not as degraded, we might say are not saved. So the Torah wrote 'sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a sentence from before. It explains why the cases of זכור and נערה המאורסה alone would not teach us about other עריות, so the Torah needed the word 'חטא'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the two cases has something extra: a male is attacked in an unnatural way, and the betrothed girl loses her virginity and is shamed. Other עריות lack these extras, so we could not learn them from these cases. The word 'חטא' fills that gap and includes every ערוה.

keyTerms.meaning: degrades, damages (here, causes her shame and loss of virginity)

phrases.english: because for this one it is not his natural way,
and that one, he degrades her.
But the other forbidden women, for whom it is their natural way,
and their degradation is not great, I would say: no.
phrases.notes: Meaning we would say the attacker may not be killed to save them.

phrases.english: So the Merciful One wrote 'sin.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכותא from before this passage, giving the reason the two explicit cases cannot teach the rest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'חטא' extends the רודף rule to all עריות, not just זכור and נערה המאורסה.

steps.title: Why the word 'death' is needed to limit the rule
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had written only 'חטא', we would include even prohibitions that are only a plain לאו. So the Torah wrote 'מות' to limit the rule to sins that carry death.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written only 'sin', I would think it covers even women forbidden by a plain prohibition. So the Torah wrote 'death.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the opposite problem. The word 'חטא' by itself is too broad, so the Torah added 'מות' to narrow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חטא' alone could mean any sin at all, even a simple לאו. 'מות' tells us the rule only applies to relations that carry a death punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (an early, mistaken assumption)
those forbidden by a plain negative commandment (punished with lashes)

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only 'sin,'
I would have said even women forbidden by a plain prohibition.
So the Merciful One wrote 'death.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that 'חטא' from step 1 is too broad by itself and needs 'מות' to limit it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'מות' limits the rule so that it does not cover חייבי לאוין.

steps.title: Why 'sin' is still needed alongside 'death'
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had written only 'מות', we would think the rule covers only relations punished by מיתת בית דין, not those punished by כרת. So 'חטא' is needed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the Torah had written only 'death', I would say: those liable to a court death penalty, yes; those liable to כרת, no. So the Torah wrote 'sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reasoning. It shows that 'מות' by itself is too narrow, so 'חטא' is also needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מות' alone might mean only a death penalty given by בית דין. 'חטא' widens it to include relations punished by כרת. The two words balance each other: one prevents going too wide, and the other prevents going too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: those liable to a death penalty given by the court
those liable to כרת, a punishment from Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: It may look like a circle, since 'חטא' is explained by 'מות' and 'מות' by 'חטא'. It is not a circle: each word fixes a different gap in the other, and both together give the exact scope.
steps.whatToRemember: 'חטא' + 'מות' together = all עריות punishable by death or כרת, but not plain לאוין.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only 'death,'

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין – אֵין,
phrases.english: I would have said: those liable to a court death penalty, yes,
those liable to כרת, no.
So the Merciful One wrote 'sin.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא by showing that 'מות' needs 'חטא', just as 'חטא' needed 'מות'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'חטא' extends the rule to חייבי כריתות, not only to חייבי מיתות בית דין.

steps.title: Why are 'young man' and 'young woman' needed at all?
steps.stepSummary: If 'חטא מות' already covers every case, the Torah could have written just that. Why does it also need the words 'נער' and 'נערה'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the Torah write only 'sin of death', and it would not need 'young man' and 'young woman'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole build-up. If 'חטא מות' covers everything, the words 'נער' and 'נערה' look extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1-3 showed that 'חטא מות' sets the full scope of the rule. If so, the specific cases of נער and נערה seem to add nothing. The גמרא asks what they are there for.

keyTerms.meaning: young man / young woman, words in the פסוק

phrases.english: But let the Merciful One write 'sin of death,'
and it would not need 'young man' and 'young woman'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of steps 1-3 to argue that the words נער and נערה are not needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the words 'נער' and 'נערה' in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'חטא מות' alone defines the full scope, then the specific cases are extra words.

steps.title: 'Young man' and 'young woman' come to exclude idol worship, animals and שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that 'חטא מות' is enough to include all the cases. Then it explains that 'נער' and 'נערה' come to exclude: one excludes someone about to worship עבודה זרה, and the other excludes someone about to sin with a בהמה or break שבת. We do not kill such a person to stop him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is so. Then what are 'young man' and 'young woman' for? One comes to exclude one who worships idols, and one comes to exclude an animal and שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge. It then explains that the extra words are not for including cases but for excluding them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'חטא מות' covers the inclusions, 'נער' and 'נערה' teach a limit. The rule is about saving a human victim. So someone about to commit עבודה זרה, an act with a בהמה, or חילול שבת, where no person is harmed, may not be killed to prevent the sin, even though these sins carry death.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the limit of the רודף rule. We may kill to stop a sin only when a victim is being attacked, not to stop every sin that carries death.
steps.whatToRemember: 'נער' and 'נערה' exclude: עבודה זרה (one word), and בהמה and שבת (the other word). We do not kill to prevent these.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so.
But then, what are 'young man' and 'young woman' for?
One comes to exclude one who worships idols,
and one comes to exclude an animal and שבת.
phrases.notes: He means someone about to have relations with an animal, or about to break שבת. We don't kill him to stop it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by agreeing with it and giving the extra words a new job: excluding cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the point and reassigns the words: they come to exclude, not to include.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'נער' and 'נערה' are needed to include the cases of זכור and נערה המאורסה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חטא מות' covers the inclusions. 'נער' and 'נערה' exclude עבודה זרה, בהמה and שבת from the רודף rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One may not kill a person to stop him from עבודה זרה, an act with a בהמה, or חילול שבת.

steps.title: How does רבי שמעון בן יוחי use the two words?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי holds that an idol worshipper IS stopped at the cost of his life. So for him, the words נער and נערה cannot be excluding עבודה זרה. What are they for?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי שמעון בן יוחי, who says that a person about to worship idols may be stopped even at the cost of his life, why do I need the two words?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 5. That answer used one word to exclude עבודה זרה, but רבי שמעון בן יוחי does not exclude עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, one of the words came to exclude עבודה זרה. רבי שמעון בן יוחי says the opposite: we DO stop an idol worshipper at the cost of his life. So for him that exclusion does not work, and the גמרא asks what each word teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds that an idol worshipper may be stopped at the cost of his life
He may be 'saved' (stopped from sinning) even at the cost of his life
Why do I need it? (asking what a word or teaching adds)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai, who says:
one who worships idols
may be saved at the cost of his life,
phrases.notes: 'Saved' here means stopped from doing the sin, even if stopping him means killing him.

phrases.english: why do I need [the two words]?
phrases.notes: He means the two words נער and נערה from step 5.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer of step 5 against a תנא who does not exclude עבודה זרה
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that one of the words נער and נערה excludes עבודה זרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון בן יוחי holds an idol worshipper IS stopped at the cost of his life, so that word cannot be excluding עבודה זרה for him

steps.title: One word excludes בהמה, the other excludes שבת
steps.stepSummary: For רבי שמעון בן יוחי, one word excludes someone about to sin with an animal, and the other excludes someone about to desecrate שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: One word excludes a sin with an animal, and the other excludes שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: for רבי שמעון בן יוחי, the two words exclude בהמה and שבת as two separate cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since עבודה זרה is not excluded for him, both words are still free. So he splits בהמה and שבת into two separate exclusions, one for each word. This answer raises a new question, which the next step deals with: why would שבת need its own word?

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude (to take a case out of the rule)
An animal; here, someone about to sin with an animal

phrases.english: One is to exclude an animal,
and one is to exclude Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד לְמַעוֹטֵי בְּהֵמָה, וְחַד לְמַעוֹטֵי שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the two exclusions to fit this תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without עבודה זרה to exclude, the two words seem to have no job
steps.terutzMaskana: One word excludes בהמה and the other excludes שבת

steps.title: Why שבת needs its own exclusion
steps.stepSummary: We might have learned שבת from עבודה זרה, because the Torah uses the word 'desecration' for both. So a separate word is needed to exclude שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: let שבת be learned from עבודה זרה, through the word 'desecration' that appears by both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שבת needs its own word to exclude it, and why it can't just be grouped with בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses the word חילול (desecration) for both שבת and עבודה זרה. This kind of word link is a גזירה שוה. Through it we might have said that just as an idol worshipper is stopped at the cost of his life, so is a person about to desecrate שבת. The extra word blocks that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind to say (the mistaken first thought)
Desecration; a word used by both שבת and עבודה זרה
Learning one law from another because the Torah uses the same word in both places

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the sides. The גזירה שוה would have made שבת strict, like עבודה זרה for this תנא. The extra word is there to stop that and keep שבת out.

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:
let Shabbat be derived from "desecration"
"desecration" from idol worship.
phrases.notes: The same word appears by both, so we would learn one from the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: תֵּיתֵי שַׁבָּת מֵחִילּוּל חִילּוּל מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the answer in step 7 needs a separate word just for שבת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a mistaken first thought that the extra word comes to block
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבת would be learned from עבודה זרה through the shared word חילול, so a שבת desecrator would be stopped at the cost of his life
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra word teaches that a שבת desecrator is NOT stopped at the cost of his life

steps.title: What about רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who includes שבת?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון accepts the 'desecration' link and holds that a שבת desecrator IS stopped at the cost of his life. So for him, what does the second word exclude?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who says that a person about to desecrate שבת may be stopped at the cost of his life, because שבת is learned from עבודה זרה through the word 'desecration', what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third view. This view does not exclude עבודה זרה or שבת, so it asks what the two words teach for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the גזירה שוה from step 8 is actually true. That leaves only בהמה to exclude, but there are two words. So the second word seems to have no job.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of רבי שמעון; holds that a שבת desecrator may be stopped at the cost of his life
What is there to say? (how do we answer for this view?)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, who says:

phrases.aramaic: מְחַלֵּל אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נִיתָּן לְהַצִּילוֹ בְּנַפְשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: one who desecrates Shabbat may be saved at the cost of his life,
since Shabbat is derived from "desecration"
"desecration" from idol worship,
phrases.notes: This is the same link from step 8, but here he really holds by it.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same question to a תנא who does not exclude שבת either
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that each of the two words, נער and נערה, excludes a separate case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For this תנא only בהמה is excluded, so one of the two words has nothing to exclude

steps.title: One word excludes בהמה; the other is just a style of writing
steps.stepSummary: For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, one word excludes בהמה. The other word does not teach anything new: once the Torah wrote נער, it also wrote נערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One word excludes a sin with an animal. As for the other: since the Torah wrote נער, it also wrote נערה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that only one word teaches an exclusion. The second word comes along with the first and is not a separate teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the word is written נער but read נערה. Here the גמרא says this pair does not have to give two separate laws. One of them teaches the בהמה exclusion, and the other simply comes with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because (the Torah already wrote one thing, it wrote the other too)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on the two words: by the first answer, one word excludes עבודה זרה and the other excludes both בהמה and שבת. רבי שמעון בן יוחי excludes בהמה with one word and שבת with the other. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון excludes only בהמה, and the second word is just part of how the Torah wrote it.

phrases.english: One exclusion is to exclude an animal,
and the other —
since the Merciful One wrote "na'ar,"
phrases.notes: In the פסוק the word is written נער but read נערה; that is the 'two words' here.

phrases.english: He also wrote "na'arah."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְּידֵי דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא נַעַר, כְּתַב נָמֵי נַעֲרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Says one word is not a separate teaching; it just goes along with the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each word must teach its own exclusion
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one word teaches the בהמה exclusion; the other simply comes with it

steps.title: רבי יהודה: even when she says 'leave him alone'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא. רבי יהודה adds a case where the attacker is not killed: when the נערה המאורסה says 'leave him alone' out of fear that he will kill her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: also the girl who says 'leave him alone,' so that he will not kill her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא from earlier and quotes רבי יהודה's addition. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'also' means רבי יהודה adds a case where the attacker is NOT killed to save her. She tells the rescuers to leave him alone only because she is afraid he will kill her, not because she agrees. Even so, by רבי יהודה the attacker may not be killed in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who adds a case in the ברייתא
A betrothed young woman, the case in the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: She is not agreeing to the sin. She says 'leave him' only because she is scared he will kill her.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
also the one who says "Leave him alone"
phrases.notes: This is the betrothed girl, talking to the people coming to rescue her.

phrases.english: so that he will not kill her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הָאוֹמֶרֶת הַנִּיחוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the extra words and goes back to quote a line from the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, when a נערה המאורסה says 'leave him alone' out of fear for her life, the attacker may not be killed to stop him.

steps.title: What is the argument about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what point רבי יהודה and the רבנן disagree about in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן really depends on. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides know the basic case. The גמרא wants to find the reasoning that makes them rule differently when she says 'leave him alone.'

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the argument quoted in step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying point of disagreement between רבי יהודה and the רבנן

steps.title: רבא defines the case of the disagreement
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the case is a girl who cares about her degradation but lets the attacker proceed so he won't kill her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: They argue about a girl who cares about being degraded, but lets him go ahead so that he will not kill her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 12. רבא describes the exact case where רבי יהודה and the רבנן disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The girl has two feelings at once. She minds being degraded, but she prefers to let it happen rather than be killed. The next step shows that each side focuses on a different one of these feelings.

keyTerms.meaning: she cares about it, she is bothered by it
her degradation, the damage done to her

phrases.english: Rava says:
Where she cares about her degradation,
but she lets him, so that he will not kill her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 by defining the case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disagreement is about a girl who cares about her degradation but allows the act out of fear for her life.

steps.title: The reasoning of each side
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say the Torah cares about her degradation, and she does too. רבי יהודה says the attacker may be killed only because she would give up her life, and this girl would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: the Torah cares about the degradation, and here she does care about her degradation, so he may be stopped even at the cost of his life. רבי יהודה holds: the Torah said 'kill him' because she is ready to give up her life rather than give in. This girl is not ready to give up her life.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer by explaining why each side rules the way it does in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the reason behind the law is the degradation. Since she still cares about it, the law stays in force. For רבי יהודה, the reason is that she would rather die than be degraded. Once she prefers to stay alive, that reason is gone, so the attacker may not be killed.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'the Merciful One', meaning the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן: the law exists because of her degradation. רבי יהודה: the law exists because she is willing to die rather than give in.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
the Torah cares about the degradation,
and here she does care about her degradation.
And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
The reason the Torah said 'kill him'
is because she gives up her life to be killed rather than give in.
This girl does not give up her life to be killed.
phrases.notes: He means: she said 'leave him alone', so the reason does not apply, and he may not be killed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of both sides within the case רבא defined.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן base the law on the degradation, and רבי יהודה bases it on her willingness to die.

steps.title: A widow with a כהן גדול is also degraded
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: if degradation is the reason, a כהן גדול with a widow also degrades her, so why can't she be saved at the cost of his life?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: A כהן גדול who is with a widow also degrades her! So according to the reason of degradation, he too should be stopped even at the cost of his life.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the רבנן's reason, that the Torah cares about degradation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול who is with a widow makes her a חללה, so she can no longer marry a כהן. That is a kind of degradation. Yet the Torah does not allow saving her at the cost of his life. So 'degradation' seems to be too broad a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: a widow, who is forbidden to a כהן גדול
a woman who becomes unfit to marry a כהן

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
A widow with a High Priest:
he also degrades her!
phrases.notes: He makes her a חללה, so she can no longer marry any כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל נָמֵי קָא פָגֵים לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the רבנן's reason given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's reason that the Torah cares about degradation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A widow with a כהן גדול is also degraded, yet he may not be killed to stop him. So degradation alone cannot be the reason.

steps.title: Only a big degradation counts
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the Torah cares about a big degradation, not a small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The Torah cares about a big degradation. It does not care about a small degradation.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא's challenge by limiting which kind of degradation counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cases in the ברייתא carry a big degradation. A widow with a כהן גדול is only a small degradation, because she just becomes unfit for כהונה. So the Torah's concern, and the permission to stop the attacker at the cost of his life, applies only to the big kind.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, the Torah's concern is a big degradation, not every degradation.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The Torah cares about a big degradation;
the Torah does not care about a small degradation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַפִּיגְמָא רַבָּה קָפֵיד רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the principle by drawing a distinction of degree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any degradation, even becoming a חללה, would allow killing the attacker.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a big degradation is the Torah's concern. Becoming a חללה is a small degradation and does not count.

steps.title: Back to the ברייתא: 'sin' means חייבי כריתות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again: the word 'חטא' refers to women forbidden under penalty of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'Sin' refers to those forbidden under penalty of כרת. So a man trying to force such a woman may be stopped even at the cost of his life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to another line of the ברייתא. It quotes this line to set up the contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line widens the law beyond a נערה המאורסה. Anyone attacking a woman forbidden to him under כרת may be stopped at the cost of his life. This is the rule the next step will test.

keyTerms.meaning: sin, the word in the פסוק that the ברייתא explains

phrases.english: 'Sin':
these are those liable to karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יהודה discussion and returns to another clause of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An attacker of a woman forbidden to him under כרת may be stopped even at the cost of his life.

steps.title: Contradiction: a man who rapes his sister pays a fine
steps.stepSummary: A משנה lists a man who rapes his sister as paying a קנס. But if he may be killed to stop him, he should be exempt from paying.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא sets up a contradiction: A משנה teaches, 'These are the girls who receive a קנס: one who is with his sister.' But his sister is forbidden under כרת, so he may be killed to stop him. Someone who may be killed for an act does not pay money for it. So how can he pay a קנס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the rule from step 17 seems to clash with a משנה about the קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a person who becomes liable to death for an act is exempt from paying for that same act. Since a brother attacking his sister may be killed, he should not have to pay. Yet the משנה says he does pay a קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: and they pointed out a contradiction
a fixed fine paid by a rapist to the girl's father
one who is with his sister

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say the hidden rule out loud: someone liable to death for an act does not also pay money for it. Without that rule, there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
And these are the girls who receive a fine:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in כתובות 29a.

phrases.english: one who is with his sister.
phrases.notes: The question is left unsaid: if he may be killed to stop him, why does he pay?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ: וְאֵלּוּ נְעָרוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן קְנָס – הַבָּא עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that an attacker of a חייבי כריתות woman may be killed to stop him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone liable to death is exempt from paying. So a brother who rapes his sister should not pay a קנס, yet the משנה says he does.

steps.title: Death-liability ends before the payment begins
steps.stepSummary: Before רב חסדא, the Sages answered: he is free of being killed from the first moment of contact, but he only owes money at the end of the act. So the two never happen at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said before רב חסדא: From the moment of first contact, once he has already degraded her, he is no longer subject to being killed. But he does not owe money until the act is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 18 by showing that the two liabilities happen at different moments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission to kill him exists only to stop the act. Once the first contact happens and the degradation is done, that permission ends. The קנס only becomes due at the end of the act. Since he is never liable to death and to payment at the same moment, the exemption does not apply, and he pays.
steps.whatToRemember: The Sages' first answer: the killing permission ends at the first contact, and the קנס starts only at the end. The next step shows this works only for one view of what הערה is, so רב חסדא and רבא give other answers.

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rav Ḥisda:
From the moment of first contact, when he has degraded her,
he is already free from being killed.
Money he does not pay
until the end of the act.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא: מִשְּׁעַת הַעֲרָאָה דְּפַגְמַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates the two liabilities by timing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Death-liability and the money obligation happen together, so he should be exempt from the קנס.
steps.terutzMaskana: The death-liability ends at the first contact, and the money obligation starts only at the end, so he pays the קנס.

steps.title: רב חסדא shows the Sages' answer only works by one opinion
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the Sages' answer works if הערה means outside contact only. But if הערה means the first entry, she already loses her בתולים at that moment, so the danger of death and the קנס would come together.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says the first stage is only a 'kiss.' But for the one who says the first stage is entering partway, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks the answer the Sages just gave him in Step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages said that once first contact happens he can no longer be killed, but he owes money only at the end of the act. If the first stage is just outside touching, that works. But if the first stage already takes away her בתולים, the קנס starts at the same moment he can be killed, and the problem returns.

keyTerms.meaning: Entering partway, the first real entry
What is there to say? (the answer fails)

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says:
the first stage of relations is a 'kiss,'
phrases.notes: He means only outside touching, without really going in.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says:
the first stage is entering partway,
phrases.notes: At this point she is already no longer a virgin, so the fine would start right away.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 19 by showing it depends on one side of a dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Sages' answer that the danger of death and the קנס never happen at the same moment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If הערה is the first entry, she loses her בתולים right then, so he owes the קנס at the very moment he may be killed.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the first act was not the usual way
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא gives his own answer: the משנה speaks of a case where the brother first came on her not the usual way, then later the usual way. The קנס comes only from the second act, when he could no longer be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: for example, he first came on her in an unusual way, and then came on her again in the usual way.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the Sages' answer failed, רב חסדא gives a new case to explain the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first, unusual act already degraded her, so that is when he could be killed to stop him. But she was still a בתולה, so no קנס yet. The second, usual act took her בתולים and made him owe the קנס, but by then she was already degraded, so he could not be killed. The two never overlap.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the old answer for a new one)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two moments: the death danger was at the first act, and the קנס came only at the second act.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said:
for example, where he came on her in an unusual way,
phrases.notes: After this she is already degraded, but she is still a virgin.

phrases.english: and then came on her again in the usual way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 19 with a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a special case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה was a simple case where the danger of death and the קנס come together.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is a case of two acts: the first brought the danger of death, the second brought the קנס.

steps.title: רבא: the sister let him, following רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers differently: the משנה speaks of a sister who let her brother go ahead so he would not kill her. In that case he may not be killed, so he pays the קנס. This follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is where she lets him, so that he won't kill her, and this follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, different answer to the question from Step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not split the act into two moments. He says that in the משנה's case he could never be killed at all, because she gave in so he would not kill her. With no death danger, nothing stops the קנס. This works only by רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: So that he won't kill her

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers for the brother who pays a קנס: רב חסדא says the death danger and the קנס came from two separate acts. רבא says he was never in danger of death, because she gave in, following רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
it is where she lets him, so that he won't kill her,
and this follows Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה holds that when she gives in like this, we don't save her by killing him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of Step 18, alongside רב חסדא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a special case, following one תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought every brother in this case could be killed to stop him, so he should never pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the sister gives in so he won't kill her, by רבי יהודה he may not be killed, so he pays the קנס.
